- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and model forecasts rise, reduce forecast by 1–4% to avoid overreaction.
- Model often underestimates true price peaks in early 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for days 1–5 if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >2% for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
